AB-01.reason: Triangulating a WallSurface breaks export: all triangles share one gml_polygon_id, the exporter groups them into one polygon and (on Railway v3) refuses the result as a degenerate ring. Desired: same polygon id, valid polygon, no interior rings

AB-02.reason: Deleting a Window object leaves its wall interior ring: on Railway v3 the wall still exports 5 rings for 2 openings instead of 4, with no warning. This check exercises a plain legacy import with no experimental-authoring-core record (bpy.data.objects.remove on an imported, never-authored Window) - genuinely unfixed by design (CAC-P4.4): there is no record on that object for any guard to protect, so there is nothing to route or block. The record-backed case is fixed: cgml.delete_feature (P3.4) routes an explicit delete correctly, and native X/Delete on a record-backed Window is now blocked or routed through delete_feature by the CAC-P4.4 guarded-delete keymap wrapper (D-7a) rather than merely detected at export pre-flight (P3.3's dangling_ring stays as the last-resort net for anything that still bypasses the UI, e.g. a raw bpy.data.objects.remove from a script)
AB-02.fixed_in: P3.4 (record-backed via cgml.delete_feature), P4.4 (record-backed via native X/Delete - blocked/routed, D-7a); the legacy/no-record path this check exercises stays open by design, not a P4 target

AB-03.reason: Semantic Stamp copies the source mesh; a flat source gives a flat stamped Window coplanar with the solid wall (V1)

AB-04.reason: Draw with depth 0 leaves a flat fill coplanar with the wall (_make_centered_prism returns early, V3)

AB-05.reason: CityGML 2 import never applies synthetic opening depth: a flat source opening stays flat (Railway v2 Door), while the same id from CityGML 3 gets 0.04 m (V2)

AB-06.reason: split_into_semantic_surfaces with a non-identity Building transform applies the transform twice (no matrix_parent_inverse, V8); Railway v3 geometry moves by up to ~196 m

AB-15.reason: AB-15b (legacy/flag-off Shift+D; P4.10 split): duplicating a record-less object with the authoring-core flag off gives two objects with one gml_id and the export corrupts or loses data: CityGML 2 folds the copy's face into the original wall polygon as an interior ring (hole = outline, xmllint passes); CityGML 3 drops the copy without refusing or warning. Both checks import Railway v3 with the flag popped and Shift+D a legacy WallSurface that carries no record. Checks are policy-neutral: export may refuse or write the copy, never corrupt or drop silently. AB-15a, the record-backed Shift+D of a Window, is fixed by the D-4 policy (P4.7: export pre-flight refuses the unresolved collision, cgml.initialize_duplicate re-mints identity, ring and record; v2/v3 export evidence in test_cac_p4_duplicate_identity)
AB-15.fixed_in: AB-15a: P4.7 (D-4). AB-15b: unscheduled - legacy/flag-off path, not a record-backed P4 contract item
